claim: Unprompted GPT-4 idea pools are less diverse than human group pools
quote: pools of ideas generated by GPT-4 with various plausible prompts are less diverse than ideas generated by groups of human subjects

claim: Chain-of-thought prompting gave the most diverse AI idea pool, near human groups
quote: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting leads to the highest diversity of ideas of all prompts we evaluated and was able to come close to what is achieved by groups of human subjects

claim: LLMs fixate: early outputs constrain later ideas
quote: LLMs exhibit fixation just as humans do, where early outputs constrain subsequent ideation

claim: Personas widen coverage but amplify fixation; CoT plus personas gives the highest diversity
quote: Persona modifiers based on ordinary individuals improve knowledge partitioning but amplify fixation. This fixation can be mitigated by using chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, and combining both strategies produces the highest idea diversity, outperforming humans

claim: Over-generating ideas mostly yields duplicates even when told to avoid repeats
quote: This leaves about 5% non-duplicated ideas out of all the generated seed ideas

claim: Across studies, AI ideas are less novel per idea and less diverse as a set
quote: AI-generated ideas are less novel at the idea level and less diverse at the set level

claim: Pooling across vendors, CoT, and heterogeneous personas or constraints restore diversity
quote: pooling ideas across vendors; prompt engineering, including Chain-of-Thought prompting and injecting heterogeneous personas or constraints

claim: Meta-analysis: interactive brainstorming groups produce fewer and worse ideas than nominal groups
quote: Generally, brainstorming groups are significantly less productive than nominal groups, in terms of both quantity and quality

claim: Work alone first, then together (hybrid) beats pure team work on quantity, quality and picking the best
quote: groups employing the hybrid process are able to generate more ideas, to generate better ideas, and to better discern their best ideas compared to teams that rely purely on group work

claim: Large electronic groups can out-generate nominal groups (a different condition)
quote: large electronic groups can facilitate the number of ideas generated relative to control groups of similar numbers of solitary performers (nominal groups)

claim: Premortem reduced plan confidence more than other methods (method authors)
quote: the Premortem method, imagining that a plan has failed and then generating reasons to explain why, reliably reduced confidence more than each of the other conditions

claim: The source study for prospective hindsight found little effect of temporal perspective; certainty of the outcome drove the explanations
quote: In the first experiment, temporal perspective showed little influence while outcome uncertainty strongly affected the nature of explanations for events

claim: LLM ideas were judged more novel but slightly less feasible than expert ideas
quote: LLM-generated ideas are judged as more novel (p < 0.05) than human expert ideas while being judged slightly weaker on feasibility

claim: LLM self-evaluation of ideas failed in the ideation agent
quote: failures of LLM self-evaluation and their lack of diversity in generation

claim: Without external feedback LLM self-correction fails and can degrade answers
quote: LLMs struggle to self-correct their responses without external feedback, and at times, their performance even degrades after self-correction

claim: Self-feedback refinement produced outputs that humans and automatic metrics preferred, with task performance about 20% (absolute) higher on average (output polish, not judgment accuracy)
quote: outputs generated with Self-Refine are preferred by humans and automatic metrics over those generated with the same LLM using conventional one-step generation

claim: Multi-agent debate does not reliably beat self-consistency or ensembling
quote: multi-agent debating systems, in their current form, do not reliably outperform other proposed prompting strategies, such as self-consistency and ensembling using multiple reasoning paths

claim: Tuned debate setups can do better
quote: when performing hyperparameter tuning, several MAD systems, such as Multi-Persona, perform better

claim: Across 9 benchmarks debate often fails to beat CoT and self-consistency at higher cost
quote: MAD often fail to outperform simple single-agent baselines such as Chain-of-Thought and Self-Consistency, even when consuming significantly more inference-time computation

claim: Mixing different models is reported to improve debate frameworks (one source)
quote: explore the role of model heterogeneity and find it as a universal antidote to consistently improve current MAD frameworks

claim: Consider-the-opposite corrected bias more than instructions to be fair and unbiased
quote: In both experiments the induction of a consider-the-opposite strategy had greater corrective effect than more demand-laden alternative instructions to be as fair and unbiased as possible

claim: A second estimate drawing on different knowledge, averaged with the first, reduces error
quote: it should be possible to reduce a person's error by averaging his or her first estimate with a second one that harks back to somewhat different knowledge

claim: Trying harder to consider the opposite can entrench the first judgment
quote: Ironically, the more people try to consider the opposite, the more they often convince themselves that their initial judgment was right on target

claim: Alternative-generation debiasing works only when generating alternatives feels easy
quote: Such strategies only work when generating alternatives is experienced as easy

claim: ACH showed mixed debiasing and may add inconsistency and error
quote: There was mixed evidence for ACH's ability to reduce confirmation bias, and we observed that ACH may increase judgement inconsistency and error

claim: ACH had no significant effect on serial position or confirmation bias
quote: ACH had no statistically significant mitigative impact on the proportion of participants that exhibited serial position effects or confirmation bias
